'''Arthur Matthews''' (1848 – 1911) was a founding professor at [[Rhodes University]] in [[Grahamstown]], South Africa.

==Early life==
Matthews was born in [[Torquay]], England in 1848 to John Redaway and Agnes Mudge Matthews.  He studied at [[Sidney Sussex College, Cambridge]] where he obtained the degrees Bachelor of Arts (BA) in 1870 and Master of Arts (MA) in 1873. He later obtained a Bachelor of Science (BSc) degree from the [[University of London]].

==Cape Colony==
He came to the [[Cape Colony]] in 1875 as the first lecturer in mathematics and physical science at [[St. Andrew's College, Grahamstown]], and later became professor and vice-principal of its College Department.{{sfn|Laurie|1914|p=18}} He built up at a Land Survey Department while at St. Andrew's College and trained many of South Africa's early land surveyors, including four [[Surveyor General|Surveyors General]].{{sfn|Currey|1955|p=32}}{{sfn|Poland|2008|p=73}}

In 1904 Rhodes University College was established and its first four professors appointed from the staff of St. Andrew's College.{{sfn|Neville|Buckland|2004|p=1}} One of these was Matthews, who became professor of mathematics and chairman of the university senate.{{sfn|Currey|1970|p=25}}

Matthews retired from Rhodes University in 1910 and died in the [[Cape Province]] in 1911.
